g.federal: A system where power is divided between the Union (Centre) and the States by the Constitution. India is a "Union of States" (Art. 1): federal in structure but with a strong Centre and unitary features (single citizenship, All India Services, emergency powers), so it is often called quasi-federal.
g.federation: A system where power is divided between the Union (Centre) and the States by the Constitution. India is a "Union of States" (Art. 1): federal in structure but with a strong Centre and unitary features (single citizenship, All India Services, emergency powers), so it is often called quasi-federal.
g.federalism: A system where power is divided between the Union (Centre) and the States by the Constitution. India is a "Union of States" (Art. 1): federal in structure but with a strong Centre and unitary features (single citizenship, All India Services, emergency powers), so it is often called quasi-federal.
g.quasi-federal: Federal in form but with a strong unitary bias, as K.C. Wheare described India: the Centre has more powers, can form or alter States (Art. 3) and takes over in emergencies.
g.unitary: A system where all power rests with one central government. India's Constitution has unitary features (single Constitution, single citizenship, integrated judiciary, emergency provisions) within a federal structure.
g.sovereign: Free to decide its own internal and external affairs, not subject to any outside authority. The Preamble declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
g.socialist: In the Preamble (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976): India's goal of ending inequality of income, status and opportunity through a mixed economy - "democratic socialism", not state ownership of everything.
g.secular: In the Indian sense (added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment, 1976): the State has no religion of its own and treats all religions equally ("sarva dharma sambhava"), rather than keeping fully separate from religion as in the West.
g.democratic: Government by elected representatives of the people with universal adult franchise; in India it covers political, social and economic democracy.
g.republic: A State whose head is elected, not hereditary. India's President is elected indirectly for five years.
g.preamble: The introduction to the Constitution, based on Nehru's Objectives Resolution (1946). It states the source of authority (We, the People), the nature of the State and its objectives (justice, liberty, equality, fraternity). Part of the Constitution (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973) but not enforceable in court.
g.constitution: The supreme law of India, adopted on 26 November 1949 and in force from 26 January 1950, framed by the Constituent Assembly.
g.constituent assembly: The body that framed India's Constitution (1946-49), set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan; Dr Rajendra Prasad was President and Dr B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
g.fundamental rights: Basic rights in Part III (Arts. 12-35) of the Constitution, enforceable in courts (Art. 32, Art. 226); the State cannot take them away except as the Constitution allows.
g.fundamental right: Basic rights in Part III (Arts. 12-35) of the Constitution, enforceable in courts (Art. 32, Art. 226); the State cannot take them away except as the Constitution allows.
g.fundamental duties: Duties of citizens in Part IVA (Art. 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice; now 11. Not enforceable in court.
g.fundamental duty: Duties of citizens in Part IVA (Art. 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice; now 11. Not enforceable in court.
g.directive principles: Guidelines for the State in Part IV (Arts. 36-51) to build a welfare State, taken from the Irish Constitution. Not enforceable in court but "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Art. 37).
g.dpsp: Guidelines for the State in Part IV (Arts. 36-51) to build a welfare State, taken from the Irish Constitution. Not enforceable in court but "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Art. 37).
g.directive principles of state policy: Guidelines for the State in Part IV (Arts. 36-51) to build a welfare State, taken from the Irish Constitution. Not enforceable in court but "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Art. 37).
g.basic structure: The doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973) that Parliament may amend any part of the Constitution but cannot destroy its basic features, such as supremacy of the Constitution, federalism, secularism and judicial review.
g.judicial review: The power of the Supreme Court and High Courts to strike down laws and executive actions that go against the Constitution; part of the basic structure.
g.writ: A court order to enforce rights. The Supreme Court (Art. 32) and High Courts (Art. 226) can issue habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.
g.habeas corpus: "To have the body": a writ ordering a person who has been detained to be produced before the court, so the court can check whether the detention is lawful.
g.mandamus: "We command": a writ ordering a public official or body to do a duty it has failed to do.
g.certiorari: A writ by which a higher court quashes an order of a lower court or tribunal passed without jurisdiction or in error.
g.quo warranto: "By what authority": a writ asking a person to show by what right they hold a public office.
g.prohibition: (As a writ) an order of a higher court stopping a lower court or tribunal from going beyond its jurisdiction.
g.ordinance: A temporary law made by the President (Art. 123) or a Governor (Art. 213) when the legislature is not in session; it lapses six weeks after the legislature reassembles unless approved.
g.money bill: A Bill only on taxes, borrowing and the Consolidated Fund (Art. 110). It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha; the Speaker certifies it, and the Rajya Sabha can only delay it for 14 days.
g.finance bill: A Bill on revenue or expenditure that is not purely a Money Bill; it needs the President's recommendation and follows the ordinary procedure in the Rajya Sabha.
g.joint sitting: A sitting of both Houses of Parliament called by the President (Art. 108) to settle a deadlock on an ordinary Bill; the Speaker presides. Not allowed for Money Bills or Constitutional Amendment Bills.
g.zero hour: The time right after Question Hour in Parliament when members raise urgent matters without prior notice; an Indian innovation (1962), not in the Rules.
g.question hour: The first hour of a sitting of Parliament, when members ask ministers questions (starred - oral; unstarred - written answers; short notice).
g.no-confidence motion: A motion in the Lok Sabha that the Council of Ministers has lost the House's support; needs 50 members to admit it, and if passed the government must resign (Art. 75: collective responsibility).
g.censure motion: A motion criticising particular policies or actions of the government; it must state reasons, and passing it does not force the government to resign.
g.adjournment motion: A motion in the Lok Sabha to set aside normal business and discuss an urgent matter of public importance; needs 50 members' support.
g.whip: A party official, and the written order they issue, telling party MPs or MLAs how to vote; defying it can lead to disqualification under the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule).
g.anti-defection law: The Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985): MPs and MLAs who leave their party or defy its whip can be disqualified by the Speaker/Chairman; merger of two-thirds of a party is exempt.
g.president's rule: Central rule in a State under Art. 356 when its government cannot be run as per the Constitution; approved by Parliament within two months, for up to three years. Limited by S.R. Bommai (1994).
g.emergency: Special powers in Part XVIII: National Emergency (Art. 352: war, external aggression, armed rebellion), President's Rule (Art. 356) and Financial Emergency (Art. 360, never used).
g.governor: The constitutional head of a State, appointed by the President for five years (holds office at the President's pleasure); acts on the advice of the State Council of Ministers except in discretionary matters.
g.speaker: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha (or a State Assembly), elected by its members; decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill and on disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
g.attorney general: The Government of India's chief legal adviser (Art. 76), appointed by the President; may speak in Parliament but cannot vote.
g.comptroller and auditor general: The auditor of all receipts and spending of the Union and States (Art. 148), appointed by the President for six years or until age 65; called the guardian of the public purse.
g.cag: The auditor of all receipts and spending of the Union and States (Art. 148), appointed by the President for six years or until age 65; called the guardian of the public purse.
g.finance commission: A body set up by the President every five years (Art. 280) to recommend how taxes are shared between the Centre and the States and grants-in-aid to States.
g.election commission: The constitutional body (Art. 324) that conducts elections to Parliament, State legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.
g.panchayati raj: The three-tier system of rural local self-government (village, block, district) given constitutional status by the 73rd Amendment (1992), Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).
g.gram sabha: All registered voters of a village panchayat area; under PESA it has special powers over land, resources and customs in Scheduled Areas.
g.municipality: An urban local body; the 74th Amendment (1992) gave them constitutional status (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects).
g.scheduled caste: Communities notified by the President under Art. 341 as having suffered untouchability; given reservations and protection under the Constitution.
g.scheduled castes: Communities notified by the President under Art. 341 as having suffered untouchability; given reservations and protection under the Constitution.
g.scheduled tribe: Tribal communities notified by the President under Art. 342; protected through reservations and the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
g.scheduled tribes: Tribal communities notified by the President under Art. 342; protected through reservations and the Fifth and Sixth Schedules.
g.scheduled area: Tribal areas declared by the President under the Fifth Schedule, with a Tribes Advisory Council and special powers for the Governor.
g.scheduled areas: Tribal areas declared by the President under the Fifth Schedule, with a Tribes Advisory Council and special powers for the Governor.
g.reservation: Seats kept aside in legislatures, education and government jobs for SCs, STs, OBCs and EWS (Arts. 15(4), 16(4), 330, 332); capped at 50% by the Indra Sawhney case (1992), except EWS.
g.creamy layer: The better-off section of the OBCs who are excluded from reservation benefits (Indra Sawhney, 1992), set by an income limit.
g.dyarchy: Dual government: introduced in the provinces by the Government of India Act 1919 (reserved subjects under the Governor, transferred subjects under Indian ministers) and planned at the Centre by the 1935 Act.
g.diarchy: Same as dyarchy: dual government, introduced in the provinces by the Government of India Act 1919.
g.paramountcy: The British Crown's supreme authority over the Indian princely states, which lapsed in 1947 when they could join India or Pakistan.
g.doctrine of lapse: Lord Dalhousie's policy (1848-56) of annexing a princely state when its ruler died without a natural heir (adopted heirs were not recognised); Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur were taken.
g.subsidiary alliance: Lord Wellesley's system (1798): Indian rulers kept a British army at their own cost and a British Resident at court and could not deal with other powers; Hyderabad was the first to accept.
g.permanent settlement: Cornwallis's land revenue system (1793) in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha: zamindars became owners and paid a fixed revenue to the Company forever.
g.ryotwari: A land revenue system (Thomas Munro, Madras; also Bombay) where the cultivator (ryot) paid revenue directly to the government.
g.mahalwari: A land revenue system (Holt Mackenzie, 1822; North-West Provinces, Punjab) where revenue was fixed on the whole village (mahal), collected through the headman.
g.swadeshi: "Of one's own country": the movement (from 1905, against the partition of Bengal) to use Indian goods and boycott British ones.
g.satyagraha: Gandhi's method of non-violent resistance - "insistence on truth" - first used in South Africa and then at Champaran (1917).
g.civil disobedience: Gandhi's movement (1930-34), begun with the Dandi Salt March, of openly breaking unjust laws non-violently.
g.varna: The fourfold division of Vedic society: Brahmana, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra.
g.jati: A hereditary caste group based on birth and occupation, the working unit of the caste system.
g.sangam: The assemblies of Tamil poets at Madurai under Pandya patronage, which produced the Sangam literature (about 300 BCE - 300 CE).
g.satavahana: The dynasty that ruled the Deccan, including Andhra, after the Mauryas (about 1st century BCE - 3rd century CE); capitals at Pratishthana and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka.
g.satavahanas: The dynasty that ruled the Deccan, including Andhra, after the Mauryas (about 1st century BCE - 3rd century CE); capitals at Pratishthana and Amaravati/Dhanyakataka.
g.monsoon: The seasonal reversal of winds that brings India most of its rain: the South-West monsoon (June-September) and the retreating North-East monsoon (October-December), which rains on Tamil Nadu and coastal Andhra.
g.kharif: The crop season sown with the South-West monsoon (June-July) and harvested in September-October: rice, maize, cotton, groundnut, jowar.
g.rabi: The crop season sown in October-November and harvested in March-April: wheat, gram, mustard, barley.
g.zaid: The short summer crop season between rabi and kharif (March-June): watermelon, cucumber, fodder crops.
g.doab: The land between two rivers that meet, such as the Ganga-Yamuna doab or the Krishna-Tungabhadra (Raichur) doab.
g.ghat: The Western and Eastern Ghats: the mountain ranges along India's west and east coasts; also steps leading down to a river.
g.ghats: The Western and Eastern Ghats: the mountain ranges along India's west and east coasts; also steps leading down to a river.
g.mangrove: Salt-tolerant forests of tidal coasts and deltas; in Andhra Pradesh at the Godavari and Krishna deltas (Coringa).
g.mangroves: Salt-tolerant forests of tidal coasts and deltas; in Andhra Pradesh at the Godavari and Krishna deltas (Coringa).
g.biosphere reserve: A large protected area under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere programme with a core, buffer and transition zone; India has 18 (Seshachalam in Andhra Pradesh).
g.national park: A protected area where no human activity like grazing or private rights is allowed, declared under the Wildlife Protection Act 1972.
g.wildlife sanctuary: A protected area for wildlife where some human activities (like grazing) may be permitted, under the Wildlife Protection Act 1972.
g.tiger reserve: A protected area for tigers under Project Tiger (1973), notified under the Wildlife Protection Act; Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam is India's largest.
g.inflation: A general rise in prices over time. In India it is measured mainly by the Consumer Price Index (CPI); the RBI targets 4% CPI inflation (band of 2-6%).
g.repo rate: The rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks against government securities; the main tool of monetary policy, set by the Monetary Policy Committee.
g.reverse repo rate: The rate at which the RBI borrows money from banks; since 2022 the Standing Deposit Facility is the floor of the policy corridor.
g.crr: The share of a bank's deposits that it must keep as cash with the RBI, earning no interest.
g.cash reserve ratio: The share of a bank's deposits that it must keep as cash with the RBI, earning no interest.
g.slr: The share of a bank's deposits that it must keep in cash, gold or government securities itself.
g.statutory liquidity ratio: The share of a bank's deposits that it must keep in cash, gold or government securities itself.
g.fiscal deficit: The government's total borrowing need in a year: total expenditure minus revenue receipts and non-debt capital receipts. The FRBM target for the Centre is 3% of GDP.
g.revenue deficit: Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts: shows how much the government borrows to meet day-to-day spending.
g.primary deficit: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments: the borrowing needed apart from paying interest on past debt.
g.gdp: The value of all final goods and services produced within the country in a year. India's base year is 2011-12 (being revised).
g.gross domestic product: The value of all final goods and services produced within the country in a year. India's base year is 2011-12 (being revised).
g.gst: The single indirect tax on goods and services across India since 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment), with CGST, SGST and IGST; rates are set by the GST Council.
g.goods and services tax: The single indirect tax on goods and services across India since 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment), with CGST, SGST and IGST; rates are set by the GST Council.
g.budget: The Annual Financial Statement (Art. 112): the government's estimated receipts and spending for the financial year (1 April - 31 March), presented in Parliament.
g.consolidated fund: The main account of the Government of India (Art. 266): all revenues, loans and loan repayments go into it, and no money can be spent from it without Parliament's approval.
g.contingency fund: A fund placed at the President's disposal (Art. 267) for urgent unforeseen spending, made good later by Parliament.
g.public account: The account (Art. 266(2)) for money the government holds as a banker, such as provident funds and small savings, which does not need Parliament's vote.
g.niti aayog: National Institution for Transforming India: the government's policy think tank, set up on 1 January 2015 to replace the Planning Commission; the Prime Minister is its Chairperson.
g.planning commission: The body (1950-2014) that made India's Five-Year Plans, set up by a Cabinet resolution; replaced by NITI Aayog.
g.five-year plan: India's development plans from 1951 to 2017, made by the Planning Commission; the 12th Plan (2012-17) was the last.
g.five year plan: India's development plans from 1951 to 2017, made by the Planning Commission; the 12th Plan (2012-17) was the last.
g.msp: The price at which the government promises to buy certain crops from farmers, announced for 22 crops on the advice of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
g.minimum support price: The price at which the government promises to buy certain crops from farmers, announced for 22 crops on the advice of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
g.green revolution: The rise in food grain output from the late 1960s through high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation, led by M.S. Swaminathan, mainly in wheat in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.
g.white revolution: Operation Flood (from 1970) led by Verghese Kurien, which made India the world's largest milk producer.
g.blue revolution: The growth of fisheries and aquaculture; Andhra Pradesh is India's leading producer of farmed fish and shrimp.
g.self-help group: A small group of 10-20 poor people, mostly women, who save together and take bank loans as a group; linked to banks under NABARD's programme (1992) and DAY-NRLM.
g.self help group: A small group of 10-20 poor people, mostly women, who save together and take bank loans as a group; linked to banks under NABARD's programme (1992) and DAY-NRLM.
g.shg: A small group of 10-20 poor people, mostly women, who save together and take bank loans as a group; linked to banks under NABARD's programme (1992) and DAY-NRLM.
g.mgnrega: The 2005 Act that guaranteed 100 days of paid unskilled work a year to every rural household that asked for it; replaced from 1 July 2026 by VB-G RAM G.
g.mahatma gandhi national rural employment: The 2005 Act that guaranteed 100 days of paid unskilled work a year to every rural household that asked for it; replaced from 1 July 2026 by VB-G RAM G.
g.pesa: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act 1996: extends Panchayati Raj to Fifth Schedule tribal areas with strong powers for the Gram Sabha.
g.lok sabha: The House of the People: the lower House of Parliament, directly elected, with 543 elected seats; its term is five years.
g.rajya sabha: The Council of States: the upper House of Parliament, elected by State legislatures (plus 12 nominated); a permanent House where one-third retire every two years.
g.vidhan sabha: A State Legislative Assembly, directly elected for five years.
g.vidhan parishad: The upper House in a State that has one (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Bihar, UP); created or abolished by Parliament under Art. 169.
g.legislative council: The upper House in a State that has one (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Bihar, UP); created or abolished by Parliament under Art. 169.
g.collector: The head of district administration (an IAS officer), responsible for revenue, law and order (as District Magistrate) and development.
g.district collector: The head of district administration (an IAS officer), responsible for revenue, law and order (as District Magistrate) and development.
g.mandal: In Andhra Pradesh, the administrative unit between the village and the district (since 1985, replacing taluks), headed by a Tahsildar; also the Mandal Praja Parishad.
g.tahsildar: The revenue officer in charge of a mandal or taluk.
g.zilla parishad: The district-level body of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system.
g.ex officio: By virtue of holding an office: for example, the Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
g.suo motu: "On its own motion": when a court or body acts without anyone filing a case.
g.public interest litigation: A case filed in court for the public good by any person, even if not personally affected; developed by Justices Bhagwati and Krishna Iyer in the late 1970s-80s.
g.pil: A case filed in court for the public good by any person, even if not personally affected; developed by Justices Bhagwati and Krishna Iyer in the late 1970s-80s.
g.lokpal: The anti-corruption ombudsman for the Centre under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013, covering even the Prime Minister with safeguards.
g.lokayukta: The anti-corruption ombudsman of a State; Maharashtra was the first to set one up (1971).
g.tribunal: A body set up to settle disputes in special areas (tax, service matters, environment) outside the regular courts (Arts. 323A and 323B).
g.cooperative federalism: The Centre and States working together on shared goals (for example through the GST Council and NITI Aayog).
g.competitive federalism: States competing with each other to attract investment and improve governance, encouraged through rankings by NITI Aayog and DPIIT.
g.special category status: Extra central help (90:10 funding of central schemes, tax breaks) once given to hilly, border or poor States on the Gadgil formula; ended for new States after the 14th Finance Commission. Andhra Pradesh was promised it in 2014.
g.isro: Indian Space Research Organisation, set up in 1969 (Vikram Sarabhai is called the father of India's space programme); headquarters in Bengaluru, launches from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh).
g.sriharikota: India's spaceport on Sriharikota island in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, between Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal; ISRO's launches take place here.
g.satish dhawan space centre: India's spaceport on Sriharikota island in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, between Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal; ISRO's launches take place here.
g.shar: India's spaceport on Sriharikota island in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh, between Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal; ISRO's launches take place here.
g.pslv: Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle: ISRO's workhorse rocket for low-Earth and Sun-synchronous orbits; launched Chandrayaan-1 (2008) and Mangalyaan (2013).
g.gslv: Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle: ISRO's rocket for heavier satellites to geosynchronous transfer orbit, using an indigenous cryogenic upper stage.
g.lvm3: Launch Vehicle Mark-3: ISRO's heaviest rocket; launched Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 and is meant for the Gaganyaan crewed mission.
g.gslv mk iii: Launch Vehicle Mark-3: ISRO's heaviest rocket; launched Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3 and is meant for the Gaganyaan crewed mission.
g.chandrayaan: India's Moon missions: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) found water molecules; Chandrayaan-2 (2019) orbiter works but its lander crashed; Chandrayaan-3 landed Vikram near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023 (now National Space Day).
g.mangalyaan: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (launched November 2013): India became the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt (September 2014).
g.mars orbiter mission: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (launched November 2013): India became the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt (September 2014).
g.aditya-l1: India's first solar observatory mission (launched 2023), placed in a halo orbit around Lagrange point L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth, to study the Sun.
g.aditya l1: India's first solar observatory mission (launched 2023), placed in a halo orbit around Lagrange point L1, about 1.5 million km from Earth, to study the Sun.
g.gaganyaan: India's human spaceflight programme to send astronauts to low-Earth orbit (about 400 km) on LVM3, with uncrewed test flights first.
g.navic: Navigation with Indian Constellation: India's own regional satellite navigation system (IRNSS), covering India and about 1,500 km around it.
g.irnss: Navigation with Indian Constellation: India's own regional satellite navigation system (IRNSS), covering India and about 1,500 km around it.
g.geostationary orbit: An orbit about 35,786 km above the equator where a satellite takes 24 hours to go round and so seems fixed in the sky; used for communication and weather satellites (INSAT, GSAT).
g.geosynchronous orbit: An orbit about 35,786 km above the equator where a satellite takes 24 hours to go round and so seems fixed in the sky; used for communication and weather satellites (INSAT, GSAT).
g.sun-synchronous orbit: A low orbit passing over the poles in which a satellite crosses each place at the same local time; used for remote sensing and Earth observation.
g.polar orbit: A low orbit passing over the poles in which a satellite crosses each place at the same local time; used for remote sensing and Earth observation.
g.cryogenic engine: A rocket engine that uses liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen at very low temperatures; India developed its own for the GSLV.
g.drdo: Defence Research and Development Organisation (1958), under the Ministry of Defence; develops missiles (Agni, Prithvi, Akash), radars and defence technology.
g.agni: India's family of surface-to-surface ballistic missiles developed by DRDO; Agni-V has a range of over 5,000 km.
g.brahmos: A supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India (DRDO) and Russia (NPOM); named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.
g.nuclear reactor: A device that produces heat by controlled nuclear fission to make electricity. India follows a three-stage programme (Homi Bhabha): pressurised heavy water reactors, fast breeder reactors, then thorium-based reactors.
g.three-stage nuclear programme: Homi Bhabha's plan to use India's large thorium reserves: stage 1 natural uranium in PHWRs, stage 2 fast breeder reactors (Kalpakkam), stage 3 thorium-based reactors.
g.fast breeder reactor: A reactor that produces more fissile fuel than it uses; India's 500 MW Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor is at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu.
g.thorium: A radioactive element that can be converted into nuclear fuel; India has among the world's largest reserves, in monazite sands of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
g.biotechnology: The use of living cells and organisms to make products, for example GM crops, vaccines and insulin; regulated in India by the Department of Biotechnology and GEAC.
g.gm crop: A crop whose genes have been changed in a laboratory; Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation in India (2002); GEAC approves GM crops.
g.gm crops: A crop whose genes have been changed in a laboratory; Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation in India (2002); GEAC approves GM crops.
g.genetically modified: A crop whose genes have been changed in a laboratory; Bt cotton is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation in India (2002); GEAC approves GM crops.
g.bt cotton: Cotton with a gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis that kills bollworms; approved in India in 2002, the only commercial GM crop.
g.geac: Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee under the Ministry of Environment, which approves the release of genetically modified organisms and crops in India.
g.crispr: A gene-editing tool that cuts DNA at a chosen place so genes can be changed precisely; in India genome-edited crops without foreign DNA are exempted from GM rules (2022).
g.dna: Deoxyribonucleic acid: the molecule that carries genetic information in living things, in the shape of a double helix.
g.vaccine: A preparation that trains the immune system to fight a disease; India's Universal Immunisation Programme (1985) and Mission Indradhanush give free vaccines.
g.antibiotic resistance: When bacteria and other microbes stop responding to medicines, mainly through overuse and misuse; India has a National Action Plan on AMR (2017).
g.antimicrobial resistance: When bacteria and other microbes stop responding to medicines, mainly through overuse and misuse; India has a National Action Plan on AMR (2017).
g.amr: When bacteria and other microbes stop responding to medicines, mainly through overuse and misuse; India has a National Action Plan on AMR (2017).
g.artificial intelligence: Computer systems that do tasks needing human-like intelligence; India's IndiaAI Mission (2024) funds computing power, datasets and AI startups.
g.quantum computing: Computing that uses quantum bits (qubits) to solve some problems much faster; India's National Quantum Mission (2023) runs till 2030-31.
g.semiconductor: A material such as silicon whose conductivity lies between a conductor and an insulator, used to make chips; the India Semiconductor Mission (2021) supports chip plants.
g.5g: Fifth-generation mobile network, much faster with lower delay than 4G; launched in India in October 2022.
g.blockchain: A shared digital record kept on many computers that cannot easily be changed; the technology behind cryptocurrencies.
g.fibre optics: Thin glass fibres that carry light signals over long distances by total internal reflection; the BharatNet project connects gram panchayats with them.
g.optical fibre: Thin glass fibres that carry light signals over long distances by total internal reflection; the BharatNet project connects gram panchayats with them.
g.superconductor: A material that conducts electricity with zero resistance below a certain temperature.
g.nanotechnology: Working with materials at the scale of nanometres (a billionth of a metre).
g.green hydrogen: Hydrogen made by splitting water with electricity from renewable energy, with no carbon emissions; India's National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) targets 5 million tonnes a year by 2030.
g.renewable energy: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished, such as sun, wind, water and biomass; India aims for 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.
g.solar energy: Energy from the Sun; India leads the International Solar Alliance; Andhra Pradesh has large solar parks such as Kurnool.
g.ecosystem: A community of living things together with their physical surroundings, working as one unit (a forest, a lake, a mangrove).
g.biodiversity: The variety of life (genes, species and ecosystems) in an area; India is one of 17 megadiverse countries and has 4 of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots.
g.biodiversity hotspot: A region rich in endemic species that has lost at least 70% of its original vegetation; India's are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland (Nicobar).
g.hotspot: A region rich in endemic species that has lost at least 70% of its original vegetation; India's are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland (Nicobar).
g.endemic: Found naturally in only one region; for example the Lion-tailed macaque is endemic to the Western Ghats.
g.food chain: The order in which energy passes from one organism to another as each eats the next (grass - deer - tiger).
g.food web: The network of many connected food chains in an ecosystem.
g.ozone layer: A layer of ozone (O3) in the stratosphere (about 15-35 km up) that absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays; depleted by CFCs; protected by the Montreal Protocol (1987), which India has ratified.
g.ozone: A layer of ozone (O3) in the stratosphere (about 15-35 km up) that absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays; depleted by CFCs; protected by the Montreal Protocol (1987), which India has ratified.
g.greenhouse effect: The warming of the Earth because gases like carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour trap heat; more of these gases cause global warming.
g.global warming: The rise in the Earth's average temperature due to greenhouse gases from burning fossil fuels and cutting forests.
g.climate change: Long-term change in temperature and weather patterns, now driven mainly by human greenhouse gas emissions; India's response includes the National Action Plan on Climate Change (8 missions, 2008).
g.carbon footprint: The total greenhouse gases caused by a person, product or country, measured as carbon dioxide equivalent.
g.carbon credit: A permit for one tonne of carbon dioxide that a company can sell if it cuts emissions; India launched its Carbon Credit Trading Scheme in 2023.
g.net zero: Balancing the greenhouse gases put into the air with those taken out; India's target is net zero by 2070 (announced at COP26, Glasgow, 2021).
g.paris agreement: The 2015 climate agreement to keep global warming well below 2 degrees C (aiming for 1.5 degrees C); countries set their own targets (NDCs).
g.unfccc: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992, Rio Earth Summit); its yearly meetings are the COPs.
g.cop: Conference of the Parties: the yearly meeting of countries under a UN convention, especially the climate COPs under the UNFCCC.
g.kyoto protocol: The 1997 agreement under which developed countries agreed to cut greenhouse gas emissions; it created the Clean Development Mechanism.
g.montreal protocol: The 1987 agreement to phase out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs; its Kigali Amendment (2016) also phases down HFCs.
g.ramsar: The 1971 convention (Ramsar, Iran) for the protection of wetlands; India has the most Ramsar sites in Asia, including Kolleru Lake in Andhra Pradesh.
g.ramsar convention: The 1971 convention (Ramsar, Iran) for the protection of wetlands; India has the most Ramsar sites in Asia, including Kolleru Lake in Andhra Pradesh.
g.ramsar site: The 1971 convention (Ramsar, Iran) for the protection of wetlands; India has the most Ramsar sites in Asia, including Kolleru Lake in Andhra Pradesh.
g.wetland: Land covered by water for all or part of the year, such as marshes, lakes and mangroves; Kolleru and Pulicat are major wetlands in Andhra Pradesh.
g.eco-sensitive zone: An area of up to 10 km around a protected area where activities are regulated to act as a buffer, notified by the Ministry of Environment.
g.esz: An area of up to 10 km around a protected area where activities are regulated to act as a buffer, notified by the Ministry of Environment.
g.environmental impact assessment: A study of the likely effects of a project on the environment before it is approved, required in India under the Environment Protection Act 1986.
g.eia: A study of the likely effects of a project on the environment before it is approved, required in India under the Environment Protection Act 1986.
g.iucn red list: The International Union for Conservation of Nature's list of threatened species, in categories such as Critically Endangered, Endangered and Vulnerable.
g.red list: The International Union for Conservation of Nature's list of threatened species, in categories such as Critically Endangered, Endangered and Vulnerable.
g.critically endangered: The highest risk category on the IUCN Red List before extinct in the wild; in India, for example, the Great Indian Bustard and Jerdon's courser (Andhra Pradesh).
g.project tiger: India's tiger conservation programme launched in 1973; now run by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
g.project elephant: India's elephant conservation programme launched in 1992.
g.compensatory afforestation: Planting forest to make up for forest land used for projects; the money is managed under the CAMPA Act, 2016.
g.campa: Planting forest to make up for forest land used for projects; the money is managed under the CAMPA Act, 2016.
g.acid rain: Rain made acidic by sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fuels; damages buildings (such as the Taj Mahal), soils and lakes.
g.eutrophication: The overgrowth of algae in water due to excess nutrients (fertilisers, sewage), which uses up oxygen and kills fish.
g.biomagnification: The build-up of toxic substances like DDT and mercury in higher levels of a food chain.
g.air quality index: India's index (2014) that reports air quality from Good to Severe based on eight pollutants, including PM2.5 and PM10.
g.aqi: India's index (2014) that reports air quality from Good to Severe based on eight pollutants, including PM2.5 and PM10.
g.pm2.5: Fine particulate matter less than 2.5 micrometres across, which can enter deep into the lungs; a key air pollutant in Indian cities.
g.el nino: An abnormal warming of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean that usually weakens India's South-West monsoon.
g.la nina: An abnormal cooling of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean that usually strengthens India's South-West monsoon.
g.indian ocean dipole: A difference in sea temperature between the western and eastern Indian Ocean; a positive IOD usually helps India's monsoon.
g.iod: A difference in sea temperature between the western and eastern Indian Ocean; a positive IOD usually helps India's monsoon.
g.cyclone: A strong storm system with low pressure at the centre and winds spiralling inwards (anticlockwise in the northern hemisphere); the Andhra coast is hit often, for example Hudhud (2014).
g.digital india: The government programme (2015) to make government services available online and build digital infrastructure.
g.aadhaar: A 12-digit unique identity number for residents of India based on biometric and demographic data, issued by UIDAI under the Aadhaar Act 2016.
g.upi: Unified Payments Interface (2016): India's instant mobile payment system run by NPCI, allowing transfers between bank accounts in real time.
g.jam trinity: Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar identity and Mobile phones, used together to transfer benefits directly to people (DBT).
g.direct benefit transfer: Paying subsidies and benefits straight into beneficiaries' bank accounts, cutting out middlemen (launched 2013).
g.dbt: Paying subsidies and benefits straight into beneficiaries' bank accounts, cutting out middlemen (launched 2013).
g.pm-kisan: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (2019): Rs 6,000 a year to farmer families in three instalments through DBT.
g.ayushman bharat: The national health programme (2018): health and wellness centres plus PM-JAY, health insurance of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for hospital care.
g.swachh bharat mission: The cleanliness mission launched on 2 October 2014 to end open defecation and improve solid waste management.
g.make in india: The 2014 campaign to make India a global manufacturing hub, supported by production-linked incentive (PLI) schemes.
g.startup india: The 2016 programme to support startups with easier rules, tax benefits and funding.
g.atmanirbhar bharat: "Self-reliant India": the 2020 vision and economic package to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce import dependence.
g.viksit bharat: "Developed India": the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047, the 100th year of independence.
g.smart cities mission: The 2015 mission to develop 100 cities with better infrastructure and technology-based services; Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati were selected from Andhra Pradesh.
g.amrut: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (2015): water supply, sewerage and green spaces in cities.
g.jal jeevan mission: The 2019 mission to give a functional household tap connection to every rural home.
g.g20: Group of Twenty: 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union (since 2023); India held the presidency in 2022-23 and hosted the New Delhi summit (September 2023).
g.brics: A group of major emerging economies: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, expanded from 2024 with Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia; runs the New Development Bank.
g.sco: Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (2001), a Eurasian security and economic group; India became a full member in 2017.
g.quad: The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue of India, the USA, Japan and Australia for a free and open Indo-Pacific.
g.saarc: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (1985) of eight South Asian countries; secretariat in Kathmandu.
g.bimstec: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (1997): Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
g.asean: Association of Southeast Asian Nations (1967), ten countries of South-East Asia; India's Act East Policy focuses on it.
g.act east policy: India's policy (2014, upgraded from the 1991 Look East Policy) to deepen ties with South-East and East Asia.
g.neighbourhood first: India's policy of giving priority to relations with its neighbouring countries in South Asia.
g.international solar alliance: An alliance of solar-rich countries launched by India and France in 2015 (Paris); headquarters in Gurugram, India.
g.isa: An alliance of solar-rich countries launched by India and France in 2015 (Paris); headquarters in Gurugram, India.
g.united nations security council: The UN body for international peace with 5 permanent members holding a veto (USA, Russia, China, UK, France) and 10 elected members; India seeks a permanent seat.
g.unsc: The UN body for international peace with 5 permanent members holding a veto (USA, Russia, China, UK, France) and 10 elected members; India seeks a permanent seat.
g.world bank: The international lender (1944) that gives loans and grants to developing countries for development projects.
g.imf: International Monetary Fund (1944): helps countries with balance of payments problems and monitors the world economy.
g.wto: World Trade Organization (1995, Geneva): sets the rules of international trade; India is a founding member.
